articles.title: Status Of Anthropic IPO As AI Fears Mount
articles.summary: Bloomberg's Anthony Hughes joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Anthropic is preparing for its IPO and has picked Nasdaq as its listing venue. The Claude chatbot maker is seeking to raise as much as or more than SpaceX in an IPO that could take place as soon as October, Bloomberg has reported. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Meta CEO Weighs In on AI Safety Debate

(Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: CetinLM: Breaking the Billion-Dollar AI Infrastructure Myth
articles.summary: As software engineers, we have been conditioned to accept a deeply flawed premise: that entering the Artificial Intelligence research space requires multi-billion-dollar infrastructure, massive enterprise GPU clusters, and infinite venture capital. The mainstream tech narrative has turned language model pre-training into a game of brute-force computational scale. But scale alone is not engineering. Recently, an independent research line under the architecture CetinLM proved that localized precision engineering can completely dismantle this high-capex barrier to entry. Built entirely from scratch under the corporate umbrella of Me Force Technology, the project successfully navigated past the 2.05 Billion training tokens milestone. The entire operation—from raw data engineering to the final optimization steps—is running natively inside a standard home desktop environment on a single, standalone 16GB NVIDIA RTX consumer GPU. articles.title: AI Trade Is in 'Digestion' Phase, JPMorgan's Sundar Says
articles.summary: Sitara Sundar, head of alternative investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, discusses the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade. Speaking on Bloomberg Television, she says her firm still has a constructive view on the AI industry in the long run. "We would actually start to lean more into some of the integration and the application layer of artificial intelligence," she adds. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI’s Frontier Faces Calls for Safety Slowdown
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down calls from AI for a slower pace at the frontier, arguing safety needs time to catch up with increasingly powerful models. The debate is reaching Washington and Wall Street, with AI-linked stocks under pressure as investors weigh what slower development means for the spending boom. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI Slowdown Fears Shake Wall Street
articles.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger and Isabelle Lee on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Tech stocks slide as new warnings call for slowing the AI race, while Wall Street braces for the Fed with inflation raising the stakes. Nissan's Christian Meunier says US auto tariffs were tough to navigate at first, but it helped the company expand its US footprint. Plus, Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney on reviving US trade talks. Barclays CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan on the forces squeezing global bond markets. And former DeepMind scientist Alex Turner on AI safety, while Nancy Tengler explains why the sell-off could be a buying opportunity. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: What Blockchain Still Needs to Win Wall Street
articles.summary: Kaiko CEO Ambre Soubiran joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why blockchain adoption on Wall Street is taking longer than expected. She argues the technology is ready, but tokenized markets still need trusted data, risk controls and traditional market safeguards before 24/7 trading and instant settlement can scale. (Source: Bloomberg)
